source_spans.locator: Psychological Review 114(2), published pp.245-246, abstract and opening framework: inference from one or a few positive examples by combining prior plausibility with statistical structure; graded uncertainty and sampling context are emphasized

same article, published pp.250-251, computational-level framework and Equations 1-4: candidate extensions, prior and likelihood terms, posterior weighting, and posterior-weighted probability for applying the label to a new item

same article, published p.252, probabilistic components and Equation 5: under independent random sampling from the true extension, smaller consistent candidates assign greater likelihood to the same examples, with the relative preference increasing exponentially with sample count; applicability depends on the sampling assumption

same article, published pp.253-255, Experiment 1: adult one-example versus three-example label-extension task, novel-item test set, and response-frequency pattern across subordinate/basic/superordinate matches

same article, published pp.256-260, Experiments 2-3: preschool-age participants, simplified label-extension tests, one-example versus three-example evidence, and graded versus sharpened response patterns

same article, published p.263, Figure 8 and Model Results: predicted probabilities compared with adult and child response frequencies; adult fit changes with an added basic-level prior bias, whereas child data do not require the same added bias

same article, published pp.263-266, Comparison With Other Models: separate contributions of repeated-sample likelihood weighting and posterior-weighted prediction averaging, plus limits of single-best-candidate and weak-likelihood alternatives

conditions: one or a few positive labeled examples are evaluated within a structured set of candidate extensions
likelihood-based sharpening across repeated examples is conditional on the assumed process by which labeled examples were sampled
task: infer which candidate extension a novel label may denote and decide which new objects should also receive that label
temporal_scope: conditioning is defined over the currently observed example set; the formal account does not require a particular sequential psychological update algorithm

nodes.description: structured set of candidate subsets of entities that could be the extension of the novel label
probability weights over candidate extensions before conditioning on the currently observed examples
one or more observed items that have been positively labeled
assumption about the process that generated the positively labeled examples under each candidate extension
probabilities assigned to the observed example set under each candidate extension and the assumed sampling process
probability weights over candidate extensions after conditioning prior weights on the observed example set through the candidate likelihoods
set of previously unlabeled test objects spanning multiple levels of the candidate category hierarchy
model-computed probability that the novel label should be applied to a particular new test object
empirical frequency with which participants apply the novel label to test objects at each hierarchical level

relations.description: the probability assigned to the observed examples under a candidate depends on which extension is proposed and on how examples are assumed to have been sampled
conditioned candidate weights depend jointly on prior plausibility and the likelihood assigned to the observed examples

under independent random sampling from the true extension, additional mutually consistent examples increase relative support for smaller consistent candidate extensions, sharpening the conditioned distribution
for a new test object, the predicted application probability is the summed conditioned weight of candidate extensions that contain that object
the behavioral test yields response frequencies for applying the novel label to new objects at different hierarchical levels

the model-computed probabilities reproduce major graded and sharpened response patterns in the adult and child data, while fitted prior structure differs between the reported adult and child comparisons
